[# [論文評述] Describing Nonstationary Data Streams in Frequency Domain](/file? The paper titled "Describing Nonstationary Data Streams in Frequency Domain" by Joanna Komorniczak addresses the issue of concept drift in data streams, which refers to the shifts in the underlying data distribution over time, affecting the performance of classifiers that rely on outdated information. The core contribution of this work is the introduction of the Frequency Filtering Metadescriptor (ffm), a tool designed for the unsupervised characterization of data streams by focusing on the frequency components that exhibit significant variance across the data. The proposed methodology employs techniques from signal processing, particularly the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), to analyze the data streams in the frequency domain. * For each data sample within a chunk, the FFT is performed to transform the data from the spatial domain to the frequency domain. This results in a frequency representation of the data chunk. Informative frequencies are those which contribute significantly to understanding the data stream's characteristics. 1. **Evaluating the influence of the number of frequency components (n)** on concept identification. The silhouette score was used to determine the optimal number of clusters, allowing for analysis of how effectively the ffm could detect recurring concepts in a data stream. The results indicated that ffm allows for competitive concept identification compared to PCA (Principal Component Analysis) and confirms its capability to effectively analyze high-dimensional data streams, particularly where traditional methods may struggle due to the curse of dimensionality. The technique was applied to real-world data streams derived from entomological studies, demonstrating the practical applicability of ffm in extracting meaningful patterns and handling variations in concept representation in nonstationary environments. In summary, the Frequency Filtering Metadescriptor (ffm) showcases a robust approach to analyzing nonstationary data streams in the frequency domain, benefiting from the inherent generalization capabilities of frequency analysis.

results.content: [Submitted on 7 Feb 2025]. # Title:Describing Nonstationary Data Streams in Frequency Domain. View a PDF of the paper titled Describing Nonstationary Data Streams in Frequency Domain, by Joanna Komorniczak. > Abstract:Concept drift is among the primary challenges faced by the data stream processing methods. The drift detection strategies, designed to counteract the negative consequences of such changes, often rely on analyzing the problem metafeatures. This work presents the Frequency Filtering Metadescriptor -- a tool for characterizing the data stream that searches for the informative frequency components visible in the sample's feature vector. The frequencies are filtered according to their variance across all available data batches. The presented solution is capable of generating a metadescription of the data stream, separating chunks into groups describing specific concepts on its basis, and visualizing the frequencies in the original spatial domain. The research is followed by the identification of concepts in the real-world data streams. The generalization in the frequency domain adapted in the proposed solution allows to capture the complex feature dependencies as a reduced number of frequency components, while maintaining the semantic meaning of data. In the first experiment, the data streams were characterized by various chunk sizes – from 50 to 200 samples in each chunk – and various numbers of drifts – from a single drift to nine sudden concept changes throughout the entire course of the stream. Similarly to the approach adopted in the first experiment, the obtained rep-resentation was normalized and clustered with k-means to an actual number of concepts present in the data stream, equivalent to 4 (number of drifts +1).
